answer: Model-weight fingerprinting stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent registers a hash of its model weights, so one model means one fingerprint. Second, peers send random prompts and check outputs match it, catching rented copies. Third, duplicate hashes trigger review, and clones forfeit a $25 bond. Fourth, weights re-register quarterly, so stale copies expire. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 fine-tunes at $40 each plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is a signal no copy can fake: a walnut shell looks alike until cracked, and on the horizon only real trees bear fruit.
